svg.title: Shortcut, Mirror, or Pipeline? Choosing an Integration Path
svg.desc: A decision tree that starts by asking whether the source data should stay owned and governed where it lives. If yes, and the source is a supported OneLake-compatible or cloud store, a shortcut references it with no copy. If the requirement is a continuously current operational replica, Mirroring is evaluated next, but Block Public Internet Access disables most of its connectors, which routes to Data Factory pipelines instead. If the need is controlled batch movement, transformation, or an unsupported source, a Data Factory pipeline with Copy activity or Copy job handles it. A warning node covers the Block Public Internet Access trap, and a second warning covers treating Mirroring as a change-event or disaster-recovery store.
svg.text: OneLake shortcut (virtualize) — Reference data in place; consumers see it as an ordinary OneLake folder with no copy.Shortcut vs Mirror vs Copy — the integrate-in-place-or-move decision
Fabric Atlas original diagram · decision guide · capabilities: onelake · mirroring
STEP 1 — DO YOU NEED A LOCAL COPY IN ONELAKE AT ALL?

g.text: Is the source itself queryable &
reachable, and stays authoritative?
Object store or Fabric-mirrorable engine, network reach OK

svg.text: YES — read in place
NO — need a governed local Delta copy
STEP 2 — PICK THE MODE

g.text: Virtualize — OneLake shortcut
Zero-copy reference · no ETL, no migration
Fits when
• Source is ADLS, Amazon S3, GCS, or Dataverse
• You want no data duplication and no pipeline
• Source engine keeps writing; Fabric reads live
• Metadata mirroring targets (Databricks, Dremio,
cross-tenant shares) — data stays in place
Behaviour
• Live, read-only reference; looks like a folder
• Delta targets auto-register as lakehouse tables
• Cross-cloud reads use per-workspace cache
(1–28 day retention) to cut egress
Watch
• Files >1 GB are never cached
• Limits: 100k/item, 10/path, 5-deep chains;
no space/%/+ in names; moving target breaks it
Replicate — Fabric Mirroring
Managed serverless CDC · Delta Parquet in OneLake
Fits when
• Source is a supported DB: Azure SQL/MI, SQL
Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL(prev), Cosmos DB,
Oracle, SAP, Snowflake, BigQuery(prev)
• You want a near-real-time local replica for
analytics without hand-built ETL
Behaviour
• Changes land in OneLake in as little as ~15s
• Replication compute is free; storage free to
1 TB per CU (F64 = 64 TB)
• Feeds Direct Lake, cross-DB T-SQL, GraphQL
Watch
• Source RLS/CLS/masking NOT carried over —
rebuild security at the Fabric layer

text.aria-label: Trap: treating Mirroring as an event log or DR backup

g.text: Trap: treating Mirroring as an event log or DR backup — Mirroring is a current-state replica, not a replayable event stream or a disaster-recovery copy.• Current-state replica only — not DR, not a stream
Copy — Data Factory pipeline
Explicit bulk / scheduled load · reshape on ingest
Fits when
• You must transform, curate, or reshape data
on the way in (not just mirror it 1:1)
• Source is not a shortcut target nor a supported
mirroring source
• One-time migration or scheduled batch loads
Behaviour
• Copy activity / pipeline writes Delta into the
lakehouse; you own scheduling & transforms
• Non-Delta formats must be converted to Delta
to surface through the SQL analytics endpoint
Watch
• A full second copy — you own freshness lag and
pipeline orchestration/failure handling
• Prefer shortcut/mirror first to avoid duplication

svg.text: STEP 3 — NETWORK-ISOLATION CHECK (can change the answer)

text.aria-label: Trap: Block Public Internet Access pauses Mirroring

svg.text: Trap: Block Public Internet Access pauses Mirroring — Enabling the tenant network gate silently pauses most native mirroring connectors.If Block Public Internet Access is enabled at the tenant
Most native database mirroring connectors pause and stop replicating. Only Open Mirroring, Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Managed Instance,

text.aria-label: Is this controlled batch, transform, or event-triggered movement?

svg.text: Is this controlled batch, transform, or event-triggered movement? — Route to Data Factory pipelines when a shortcut or Mirroring isn't the right fit.and SQL Server 2025 keep working under that restriction. On-premises data gateways cannot register at all under this setting —

text.aria-label: Is Mirroring viable for this source?

svg.text: Is Mirroring viable for this source? — Check supported-source list and Block Public Internet Access before committing to Mirroring.the only replacement is a VNet data gateway (requires ExpressRoute or site-to-site VPN). Factor this in before committing to mirroring.
Default order of preference
1. Shortcut if the source is object storage / Dataverse or a
metadata-mirroring target — integrate in place, zero copy.
2. Mirror if you need a governed near-real-time local replica of
Mirroring (replicate) — Continuous current-state replica of a supported operational database into OneLake Delta. a supported operational/analytical database.
Should the source stay authoritative? — Root question: reference, replicate, or copy the external data.3. Copy only when you must reshape on ingest or the source is
neither a shortcut target nor a mirroring source.
Inference — synthesises the verified fit-criteria above into an ordering.
Whichever mode you pick, the copy stays open
All three land data as open Delta Parquet in OneLake, so downstream
engines read the same one copy — Fabric T-SQL, Spark, and Analysis
Services, plus ADLS Gen2-compatible external engines like Databricks.
Expose it outward through SQL analytics endpoints, the GraphQL API,
or cross-tenant sharing — governed centrally by Purview and OneLake
security, which stay in force even across tenant boundaries.
All statements above are grounded in verified claims; see the design's source legend.
